summary: Cloud scan of https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com complete. Found 0 critical and 2 high vulnerabilities.

findings.name: Missing Permissions-Policy Header
findings.description: The Permissions-Policy header is missing from the HTTP response. This header allows a website to control browser features and APIs available to the page and its iframes, enhancing security by restricting access to sensitive browser functionalities (e.g., camera, microphone, geolocation). Its absence means the site cannot enforce these restrictions, potentially allowing embedded content or scripts to access features that are not intended.
findings.evidence: HTTP response header 'Permissions-Policy' was not found.

findings.name: Server Header Disclosure
findings.description: The 'Server' header is present in the HTTP response, disclosing information about the web server software and its version (nginx/1.18.0). This information can be used by attackers to identify known vulnerabilities specific to that server version, making it easier to craft targeted attacks.
findings.evidence: HTTP response header 'Server' found with value 'nginx/1.18.0'.

findings.name: X-Powered-By Header Disclosure
findings.description: The 'X-Powered-By' header is present in the HTTP response, disclosing information about the backend technology used (Express). This information can be used by attackers to identify known vulnerabilities specific to that technology and version, aiding in reconnaissance and targeted attacks.
findings.evidence: HTTP response header 'X-Powered-By' found with value 'Express'.

findings.vulnerability: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) / Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
findings.description: The application is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) / Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA). An authenticated user is able to access and retrieve sensitive data belonging to other users by simply incrementing or changing the 'id' parameter in the URL path. Specifically, user data for ID 2 was successfully retrieved while authenticated as user ID 1.

request_1.description: Request as authenticated user (ID 1) to access own data.

request_2.description: Request as authenticated user (ID 1) attempting to access data for ID 2.

evidence.payload_diff: Comparison of responses for /api/users/1 and /api/users/2 using the same authentication context shows that user with ID 1 successfully retrieved data belonging to user with ID 2. The 'email' changed from 'userA@example.com' to 'userB@example.com' and 'id' from 1 to 2, indicating unauthorized access to another user's profile. All response status codes were valid (200 OK).

findings.remediation: Implement robust access control checks on all API endpoints that accept object IDs as parameters. Ensure that the authenticated user is explicitly authorized to access the requested resource. This typically involves verifying the user's session against the requested resource's owner or permissions before returning any data. Do not rely solely on obscurity or client-side checks.
